attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Old Quay Harvest Run 7K, Sunday 24 October 2027

From Yuki Tanaka, Event Secretary, Old Quay Pacers

The race is a 7K with 220 runners and starts at 08:00. An ambulance from Halden Medical Transport is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

First aid
We'll have 3 first aid posts, at the start, the finish and halfway, with 10 trained first aiders between them, so nobody on the course is more than about a kilometre and a half from help. We also have two first aiders on bikes, carrying defibrillators.

Runners get an email in race week telling them to dress for the weather and to keep a phone with them if they can. Most have run with us before. The list of entrants includes an emergency contact for each runner, which is kept at the start.

Heat, cold and water
There's water every 2.5 km. We look at the forecast two days before and again two hours before. Over 28 degrees we start earlier or cut the course, and over 32 degrees we call it off. If it's cold or wet, we have foil blankets and a warm tent at the finish.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at St. Brigid's Hospital, 5 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Fenwick Street with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
Everyone at a post and both bike first aiders has a radio on our medical channel, with phones as backup. Calls for an ambulance go through our medical lead, who tells the crew which barrier to come to.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Nadia Petrov, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Old Quay Harvest Run 7K | Sunday 24 October 2027
Organiser: Old Quay Pacers
Race director: Yuki Tanaka
Reference: PH-66710

Overview
The Old Quay Harvest Run 7K is a 7K race of 7 km for 220 entrants, based in the St. Anne's District area of Port Halden. The start is at 08:00 and the course closes at 09:30.

Course
The course runs in order along Fenwick Street, Weir Street, Dyer Street, Linden Avenue and Bridge Row, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Dock Road, Ferry Road, Regent Road, High Street and Canal Road. The finish is in Exchange Square.

Course dimensions
Survey widths: Fenwick Street 11 m, Dyer Street 16 m, Bridge Row 14 m, kerb to kerb, excluding footways. Start pens sit side by side across the full carriageway, and spectators have the pavement and a grassed verge along most of the route.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Fenwick Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Old Quay website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Old Quay Harvest Run 7K
Date: Sunday 24 October 2027
Applicant: Old Quay Pacers
Prepared by: Tessera Event Transport
Issue: 1.1

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Old Quay Harvest Run 7K, a 7K race in the St. Anne's District area of Port Halden with a 08:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. We have not arranged any police attendance for this race.

We have a good working relationship with local residents. Several members walk the route the week before, noting anything that has changed, such as new roadworks, a barrier left in place, or a lane marked for cycles.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Northline Barriers.
- Fenwick Street, Glebe Road to Rope Walk: closed 06:30 to 10:00
- Weir Street, Bell Street to Cooper Street: closed 06:30 to 10:00
- Dyer Street, Glebe Road to Rope Walk: closed 06:30 to 10:00
- Linden Avenue, Glebe Road to Rope Walk: closed 06:30 to 10:00
- Bridge Row, Market Row to Hatter Street: closed 06:30 to 10:00

3. Major crossings
Busier junctions along the course will receive appropriate supervision during the event. Staffing levels will be determined by Northline Barriers on the morning, taking account of conditions at the time, with resources deployed flexibly to where they are most needed.

4. Diversions
Drivers will be advised to expect delays in the area and to allow additional time for their journeys. Advance information boards will be used where practical, and through traffic is expected to find alternative routes across the wider network.

5. Emergency vehicle access
The emergency services will be made aware of the event date and general location through the usual channels ahead of the day. Any vehicle attending an incident will be accommodated by staff on the ground as circumstances allow.

6. Notification
All frontages on the closed streets receive a letter drop 21 days before the event, with a further reminder at 7 days. Advance notice signs go up 10 days before, and bus operators have been given the closure times.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
